mainTopic: Whether a creature missing a limb still counts as a whole creature (the ant question), and whether the משנה means a spine AND a skull together or either one alone
overview: The גמרא first tries to solve an earlier question: does an ant missing a limb still count as a whole creature? רב יהודה מדיסקרתא brings a ברייתא about שרצים that plays the words "בהם" and "מהם" against each other and lands on a lentil-sized piece, the size of a חומט when it first forms. He concludes that size is a fixed tradition, so an incomplete creature should not count. רב שמעיה rejects the proof: the lentil rule may apply only to a creature that is not yet alive, so the ant question remains. Then the גמרא turns to our משנה, which says a נזיר shaves for "the spine and the skull," and asks whether both are needed together or either one is enough. רבא brings a ברייתא about a spine whose ribs were scraped off, and the גמרא infers that an unscraped spine alone is טמא, but this proof is pushed off. A second proof, from the story of the doctors who checked a box of bones, is also pushed off. Finally, the גמרא lays out רבי יהודה's list of six items that רבי עקיבא held טמא, where spine and skull appear together as one item, and begins a proof from that count that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יהודה brings a teaching about two verses on touching creeping creatures
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא opens a proof for the ant question by quoting a ברייתא. It plays two words in the פסוקים against each other: "בהם" (them) and "מהם" (of them).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה from דיסקרתא said: Come and hear. The verse says "them." You might think that means only whole creatures. So the verse says "of them," meaning part of them. If it said only "of them," you might think even a tiny part counts. So the verse says "them."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה starts bringing a proof for the open question about an ant missing a limb. He quotes a ברייתא that reads two words in the תורה against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "בהם" (them) sounds like you must touch a whole creature. "מהם" (of them) sounds like even part is enough. Each word limits the other, so the answer must be somewhere in the middle. That middle comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Them: sounds like the whole creature
Of them: sounds like part of the creature
You might have thought (a wrong idea the verse corrects)
Therefore the verse says (to correct that wrong idea)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda from Diskarta said:
Come and hear:
"Them": one might think this means all of them (whole creatures).
Therefore the verse says: "Of them."
If it said only "of them," one might think even a small part of them —
Therefore the verse says: "Them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה מִדִּיסְקַרְתָּא: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an attempt to settle the question from the previous section about an ant missing a limb.
steps.raayaObject: Whether an incomplete creature (an ant missing a limb) still counts as a creature
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the size of a שרץ needed for טומאה, based on "בהם" and "מהם"

steps.title: The middle answer is a lentil, so size is a fixed tradition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא settles the two words: you must touch a part that counts like the whole, and חכמים set it at a lentil, the size of a חומט when it first forms. רב יהודה concludes that the size is a fixed tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? A person is not טמא until he touches a part that counts like the whole. חכמים set that at the size of a lentil, because a חומט starts out at the size of a lentil. Learn from this that the size is a fixed tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the middle answer between "them" and "of them": a lentil-sized piece. רב יהודה then draws his proof, that the minimum size is a set tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lentil is chosen because that is how big a חומט is when it first forms, so a lentil is like a whole creature. רב יהודה's point is that being counted as a creature depends on a fixed measure. If so, an ant missing a limb, which is no longer complete, should not count as a whole creature.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How do the two verses fit together?
The size of a lentil
A skink, one of the eight שרצים
Learn from this
The size is a fixed tradition

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule that a piece of a שרץ the size of a lentil makes things טמא.

phrases.english: How so?
He is not impure until he touches a part of them that is like all of them.
And the Sages measured it at a lentil-size,
since a skink at the start of its formation is a lentil-size.
Learn from this that the size is a fixed tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 1 and draws the proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: That being counted as a creature depends on a fixed size, so an incomplete ant would not count
steps.raayaSupportSource: The lentil size, learned from how big a חומט is when it first forms

steps.title: רב שמעיה: the lentil rule may only be for a creature not yet alive
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה rejects the proof. The lentil size may matter only for a creature that has no soul yet. Once a creature is alive, maybe size does not matter, so the ant question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה said: We need the size, so that below a lentil it is not טמא, only when no soul has entered it yet. But once a soul has entered it, we do not need the size. So your question remains.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה pushes aside רב יהודה's proof. He says the ant question is still unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lentil size is about a creature still forming, before it is alive. A living ant missing a limb is a different case, since it already has a soul. So the ברייתא proves nothing about it, and the question is left as תיבעי.

keyTerms.meaning: We need / we require
A soul has entered it (it is alive)
Your question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the lentil size fails. The lentil rule may only apply to a creature not yet alive, so the question of an ant missing a limb stays open.

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya said:
When we require the size,
that if it is not a lentil-size it does not make impure,
that is when a soul has not entered it.
But if a soul has entered it, we do not require it.
Your question remains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמַעְיָה: כִּי בָּעִינַן שִׁיעוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יהודה's proof but does not decide the ant question either way
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lentil size may only apply to a creature that is not yet alive, while the ant is a living creature

steps.title: Does the משנה mean spine and skull together, or either one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which lists a spine and a skull as things a נזיר shaves for. It asks if the ו means 'and' (both needed) or 'or' (either one is enough).
steps.simpleTranslation: "The spine and the skull." They asked: Did we learn a spine and a skull together, or perhaps either a spine or a skull?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes words from the משנה and asks what they mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ו can mean 'and' or 'or.' If 'and,' a נזיר shaves only when both a spine and a skull are present. If 'or,' either one alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Spine
Skull
A question was asked among them
Or perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: Everyone agrees a spine and a skull are bones of a dead person. The question is whether one of them alone has the full טומאה that makes a נזיר shave, or only both together.

phrases.english: "The spine and the skull."
phrases.notes: These are the words of our משנה, from its list of things a נזיר must shave for.

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
Did we learn a spine and a skull (together),

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא: אוֹ שִׁדְרָה אוֹ גוּלְגּוֹלֶת?
phrases.english: or perhaps: either a spine or a skull?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ant question back to explaining a phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה requires both a spine and a skull together, or each one alone

steps.title: רבא brings a teaching about a spine whose ribs were removed
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא: a spine with most of its ribs scraped off is טהור, but in a grave, even broken or taken apart, it is טמא because of the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. A spine with most of its ribs scraped off is טהור. And in a grave, even if it is broken or taken apart, it is טמא because of the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts bringing a source to answer the spine-and-skull question. The גמרא is setting up the proof here; what it shows comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks about a spine by itself, with no skull mentioned. It says outright only that a spine with most of its ribs removed is טהור, and that inside a grave even a broken spine is טמא, because the grave joins the pieces together. The next step tries to infer from this that an intact spine alone would be טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Scraped off / removed
Ribs
Broken
Taken apart
Because of the grave, which joins the pieces together

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁדְרָה שֶׁגֵּירַד רוֹב עִילְעִין שֶׁבָּהּ — טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.english: A spine with most of its ribs scraped off is pure.

phrases.aramaic: וּבְקֶבֶר אֲפִילּוּ מְשׁוּבֶּרֶת אוֹ מְפוֹרֶקֶת — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: And in a grave, even if broken or taken apart, it is impure,
because of the grave.
phrases.notes: The grave holds all the bones together, so they count as one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question raised in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a spine alone, without a skull, makes a נזיר shave
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a spine with most of its ribs removed, and a spine inside a grave

steps.title: Inferring 'either one' from the scraped spine
steps.stepSummary: From רבא's ברייתא, the גמרא infers that an unscraped spine is טמא by itself. So the משנה must mean 'a spine OR a skull.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason the spine is טהור is that its ribs were scraped off. That means if it was not scraped, it is טמא by itself. Learn from this that the משנה means 'either a spine or a skull.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads between the lines of רבא's ברייתא to answer the question from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a scraped spine is טהור. The גמרא reasons backward: if scraping is what makes it טהור, then an unscraped spine on its own must be טמא, even without a skull. So one item alone is enough, and the ו means 'or.'

keyTerms.meaning: The reason; opens an inference from why a ruling was given
Was scraped (the ribs were scraped off the spine)
Learn from this; announces a conclusion drawn from a source
It teaches; what the משנה is saying

phrases.english: The reason is because it was scraped,
phrases.notes: He means the ribs were scraped off the spine, the case from רבא's ברייתא.

phrases.english: but if it was not scraped, it is impure,
learn from this:
it teaches 'either a spine or a skull.'

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּגֵירַד, הָא לָא גֵּירַד — טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא that רבא quoted in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's ו means 'or': a spine alone or a skull alone is enough.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from רבא's ברייתא that only a scraped spine is טהור.

steps.title: The ברייתא only teaches the scraped case
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ברייתא never says an unscraped spine is טמא alone. It only teaches that a scraped spine is טהור, so the question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא does not say that. This is what it teaches us: when the spine is scraped, it is טהור. The other question is still yours to ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Step 6, so this source does not settle the question. The גמרא tries another source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's goal was only to say that scraping makes a spine טהור. It was not dealing with whether an unscraped spine alone is טמא. So you cannot squeeze an answer about 'and' or 'or' out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: That it does not teach; the source never actually says it
This is what it is teaching us; the real point of the source
The other one; the other question
Let it remain a question for you; it stays unresolved

phrases.english: That it does not teach.
This is what it teaches us:
that when it is scraped, it is pure,
the other case, let it remain a question for you.
phrases.notes: 'The other case' is a spine by itself without a skull, which is the question we started with.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The ברייתא's ruling about the scraped spine still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference reads a rule into the ברייתא that it never meant to teach. Its only point was the scraped case.

steps.title: The box of bones checked by the doctors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source: רבי יהודה reports six items about which רבי עקיבא retracted, and a story where doctors checked a box of bones and found no spine from one dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, there are six things רבי עקיבא held טמא and חכמים held טהור, and רבי עקיבא changed his mind. There was a story where people brought a box full of bones to the בית הכנסת of the metalworkers and set it in the open air. תודוס the doctor came in with all the doctors and said: there is no spine from one dead person here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try again to solve the question. This step only quotes the source; the proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The box was left in the open air so it would not spread טומאה under the roof while it was being checked. The doctors ruled it טהור because no spine came from a single dead person. In the next step the גמרא draws a proof from the fact that they mentioned only a spine.

keyTerms.meaning: He took back his opinion
A box or basket
Metalworkers (a group that had its own בית הכנסת)
In the open air, not under a roof
A doctor

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Six things Rabbi Akiva declares impure
and the Sages declare pure,
and Rabbi Akiva took back his opinion.
And there was an incident where they brought a box full of bones
to the synagogue of the metalworkers,
and they placed it in the open air,
and Todos the doctor came in
and all the doctors with him,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'with him,' is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ: אֵין כָּאן שִׁדְרָה מִמֵּת אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and they said: there is no spine here from one dead person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, the גמרא brings a second source.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה means 'either a spine or a skull.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה and the story of תודוס הרופא and the box of bones.

steps.title: Inferring 'either one' from the doctors' words
steps.stepSummary: Since the doctors only said 'no spine from one dead person,' the גמרא infers that a spine or a skull from one body would have been enough, so the משנה means 'or.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it was טהור is that there was no spine from one person. But if there were either a spine or a skull from one person, a נזיר would shave for it. Learn from this that we learned 'either a spine or a skull' in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof out of the story it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doctors based their ruling only on the missing spine, as if a spine alone would have been enough to make it טמא. That suggests one item by itself counts, so the ו in the משנה means 'or.'

keyTerms.meaning: From one (dead person)
Shaves; the נזיר shaves because he became טמא

phrases.english: The reason is that there is no spine from one person.

phrases.aramaic: הָאִיכָּא אוֹ שִׁדְרָה אוֹ גוּלְגּוֹלֶת דְּמֵחֲדָא —
phrases.english: But if there is either a spine or a skull from one person,
a nazirite shaves for it,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אוֹ שִׁדְרָה אוֹ גוּלְגּוֹלֶת תְּנַן.
phrases.english: learn from this: we learned 'either a spine or a skull.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the story quoted in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That a spine alone or a skull alone is enough for a נזיר to shave.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The doctors' ruling, which mentioned only the missing spine.

steps.title: The doctors meant 'not even one of them'
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The doctors were saying: there is surely no spine and skull together from one body, and there is not even a spine alone or a skull alone from one body.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were speaking in a 'no need to say' style: no need to say there is no spine and skull from one person, but there is not even a spine from one person or a skull from one person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Step 9 by reading the doctors' words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doctors' statement does not prove that one item alone is enough. They may simply have been saying the box had less than you might think: not even one whole spine or one whole skull from a single body. So the story does not settle the question, and the גמרא tries another proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He is speaking in a 'no need to say' style: not only the obvious case, but even the less obvious one
There is not
Even

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say a spine alone is טמא. It only says the doctors' words fit either way, so the story proves nothing about 'and' or 'or.'

phrases.english: He is speaking in a 'no need to say' style:
no need to say a spine and a skull,
that there are none from one dead person,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ אוֹ שִׁדְרָה מִמֵּת אֶחָד
phrases.english: but even either a spine from one dead person
or a skull from one dead person, there is none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the story is rejected; the story itself stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The doctors' words can be read as 'not even one of them was there,' which says nothing about whether one alone is enough.

steps.title: A new proof from the count of six items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again from the list of six items that רבי עקיבא held טמא. The spine and the skull are listed together as the sixth item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the count: What are the six things רבי עקיבא holds טמא and חכמים hold טהור? A limb of a dead person made from two dead people; a limb cut from a living person made from two living people; half a קב of bones from two dead people; a רביעית of blood from two people; a bone the size of a barley grain that split in two; and the spine and the skull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new proof using the list of the six items. This step only lays out the list; the proof itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is a case where pieces from different bodies, or a split bone, are put together. Notice that the spine and the skull together count as just one item, the sixth. The גמרא will use the way the list is counted to try to answer the 'and' or 'or' question.

keyTerms.meaning: From the count; a proof from how many items are listed
A limb from a dead person
A limb cut off a living person
Half a קב of bones; an amount of bones that gives טומאה
A quarter-לוג of blood; an amount of a dead person's blood that gives טומאה
The size of a barley grain

phrases.english: Come and hear from the count:
And what are the six things
that Rabbi Akiva declares impure and the Sages declare pure?

phrases.aramaic: עַל אֵבֶר מִן הַמֵּת שֶׁבָּא מִשְּׁנֵי מֵתִים,
phrases.english: A limb from a dead person that comes from two dead people,
phrases.notes: He means pieces from two bodies that together make up one limb.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי שֶׁבָּא מִשְּׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: and a limb from a living person that comes from two people,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל חֲצִי קַב עֲצָמוֹת שֶׁבָּא מִשְּׁנֵי מֵתִים,
phrases.english: and half a kav of bones that comes from two dead people,
and a quarter-log of blood that comes from two,
and a bone the size of a barley grain that split in two,
and the spine and the skull.
phrases.notes: Count them: the spine and skull together are only the sixth item. Keep that in mind for the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story was pushed off, the גמרא goes back to the same ברייתא of רבי יהודה and tries a proof from its list of six items.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the spine and skull in the משנה count as one combined item or as two separate ones.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The list of six items in רבי יהודה's ברייתא, where spine and skull are listed together as one item.
